big_ideas.title: Equations come from balances
big_ideas.text: A rate of change equals inflow minus outflow plus generation; the ODE or PDE, its initial and boundary conditions, and its parameters all come from the physical system, and its answer must make physical sense.

big_ideas.title: The form of the equation picks the method
big_ideas.text: Order, linearity, coefficients (constant, Euler–Cauchy, analytic, singular) and forcing decide which technique works. Classify before you compute.

big_ideas.title: Linear problems superpose
big_ideas.text: Solutions of a linear homogeneous equation form a vector space; general solution = homogeneous basis + one particular solution, and independence (Wronskian, determinant) says when a basis is complete.

big_ideas.title: Eigenvalues decouple linear problems
big_ideas.text: Characteristic roots, matrix eigenvalues and Sturm–Liouville eigenvalues are one idea — find the modes, and each evolves on its own; their signs and imaginary parts set growth, decay, oscillation and stability.

big_ideas.title: Change the representation to simplify
big_ideas.text: Substitutions, power series, Laplace transforms and eigenfunction (Fourier) expansions turn a hard problem into algebra or a recurrence, solved there and transformed back.

practices.title: Model the system
practices.text: Translate a physical description into a differential equation with initial or boundary conditions; name the variables, parameters and units.

practices.title: Classify the equation
practices.text: State order, linearity, homogeneity, coefficient type, singular points or boundary type, and choose the method that fits.

practices.title: Execute the method
practices.text: Carry out the integration, algebra, recurrence, transform or eigen-decomposition without dropping terms or constants.

practices.title: Impose conditions
practices.text: Apply initial or boundary conditions to fix constants, eigenvalues or coefficients; keep the general solution until the end.

practices.title: Check the answer
practices.text: Substitute back, test limiting cases and t → ∞ behaviour, confirm independence and that the solution satisfies every condition.

practices.title: Interpret qualitatively
practices.text: Read stability, time constants, resonance and long-time behaviour off the roots or eigenvalues; sketch solutions and phase portraits; predict how a parameter change moves them.

los.do: Evaluate an integral by u-substitution, choosing u so its derivative appears in the integrand.
ek: ∫f(g(x))g′(x)dx = ∫f(u)du; a missing constant factor is fine, a missing x is not.

los.do: Evaluate an integral by parts, including tabular and cyclic (e^ax·trig) cases.
ek: ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du; LIATE picks u; cyclic integrals return to themselves and are solved algebraically.

los.do: Decompose a rational function into partial fractions (distinct, repeated, irreducible quadratic, improper) and integrate it.
ek: Divide first if improper; repeated factor (x−a)^k needs k terms; irreducible quadratic gets (Ax+B).

los.do: Convert complex numbers between rectangular, polar and exponential form.
ek: e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ; z = re^(iθ), r = |z|, θ = arg z.

los.do: Compute powers and roots of a complex number with De Moivre's formula.
ek: (re^(iθ))^n = r^n e^(inθ); n distinct n-th roots spaced 2π/n apart.

los.do: Find the complex roots α ± βi of a real quadratic.
ek: Complex roots of real polynomials come in conjugate pairs; α = −b/2a, β = √(4ac − b²)/2a.

los.do: Shift a summation index so two power series start at the same index and carry the same power of x.
ek: Replace m by m ± k and adjust the limits; the sum is unchanged.

los.do: Compute first and mixed partial derivatives of a function of two variables.
ek: Hold the other variable constant; for smooth functions u_xy = u_yx.

los.do: Find dy/dx for a curve defined implicitly by F(x, y) = c.
ek: dy/dx = −F_x / F_y.

los.do: Test whether M dx + N dy is an exact differential.
ek: Exact on a simply connected domain ⇔ ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x.

topics.title: Basic concepts, direction fields and Euler's method

los.do: Classify an ODE by order and linearity, and verify that a given function solves it.
ek: Order = highest derivative; linear ⇔ y and its derivatives appear to first power with coefficients in x only.

los.do: Sketch a direction field and solution curves from isoclines of y′ = f(x, y).
ek: Isocline f(x, y) = k has slope k everywhere; solution curves are tangent to the field.

los.do: Approximate an IVP solution with a few steps of Euler's method and estimate the error trend.
ek: y_(n+1) = y_n + h f(x_n, y_n); global error is O(h).

los.do: Solve a separable ODE explicitly where possible, including the IVP constant.
ek: g(y)dy = f(x)dx, integrate both sides; check for lost equilibrium solutions when dividing by g.

los.do: Reduce an ODE to separable form with u = y/x or u = ax + by + c, and solve it.
ek: y′ = f(y/x): y = ux ⇒ u + xu′ = f(u); y′ = f(ax + by + c): u′ = a + bf(u).

los.do: Solve an exact ODE by finding the potential u(x, y) = c, and fit an IVP.
ek: u_x = M, u_y = N; integrate one, differentiate, match the other.

los.do: Decide whether an integrating factor depending only on x or only on y exists.
ek: R = (M_y − N_x)/N a function of x alone ⇒ F(x) = exp∫R dx; R* = (N_x − M_y)/M of y alone ⇒ F(y).

los.do: Find the integrating factor and solve the resulting exact equation.
ek: Multiply by F, re-check exactness, then solve as exact.

los.do: Solve a linear first-order ODE with an integrating factor, including IVPs and forcing that matches e^(−∫p).
ek: y′ + py = r ⇒ y = e^(−h)[∫e^h r dx + c], h = ∫p dx.

los.do: Solve a linear ODE whose integrating-factor integral needs integration by parts.
ek: ∫e^h r dx often pairs a polynomial or trig with an exponential.

los.do: Reduce a Bernoulli equation to a linear one with u = y^(1−a) and solve it.
ek: y′ + py = g y^a ⇒ u′ + (1−a)p u = (1−a)g.

los.do: Identify which first-order method (separable, substitution, linear, Bernoulli, exact) solves a given ODE.
ek: Check in order: separable? linear in y? y^a term? exact? homogeneous in y/x?

los.do: Set up and solve a mixing-tank balance for concentration or mass of solute.
ek: dm/dt = (rate in) − (rate out), rate out = (m/V)·Q_out.

los.do: Model Newton's cooling and first-order decay, and extract a time constant, half-life or time to reach a value.
ek: dT/dt = −k(T − T_a); y = y_0 e^(−kt), t_1/2 = ln 2/k.

los.do: Solve the logistic equation and find its equilibria and carrying capacity.
ek: y′ = ky(1 − y/K) is separable and Bernoulli; y → K for y_0 > 0.

los.do: Find and classify the equilibria of an autonomous ODE y′ = f(y) from a phase line.
ek: f(y*) = 0; stable if f′(y*) < 0.

los.do: Decide whether an IVP has a unique solution near the initial point from the continuity of f and ∂f/∂y.
ek: f and f_y continuous on a rectangle around (x_0, y_0) ⇒ unique solution on some |x − x_0| < α.

topics.title: Homogeneous theory, reduction of order and the Wronskian

los.do: Use superposition to build a general solution from a basis and fit it to an IVP.
ek: For a linear homogeneous ODE, any combination c_1y_1 + c_2y_2 of solutions is a solution; two independent ones form a basis.

los.do: Find a second solution from a known one by reduction of order.
ek: y_2 = u y_1, u′ = U = e^(−∫p dx)/y_1² (standard form y″ + py′ + qy = 0).

los.do: Compute the Wronskian of two or three functions and use it to decide linear independence.
ek: W = det of the functions and their derivatives; W ≠ 0 somewhere ⇒ independent; for ODE solutions W ≡ 0 or never 0 (Abel).

los.do: Write the general solution of ay″ + by′ + cy = 0 for each of the three root cases of the characteristic equation.
ek: Distinct real: e^(λ₁x), e^(λ₂x); double: e^(λx), xe^(λx); complex α ± iβ: e^(αx)cos βx, e^(αx)sin βx.

los.do: Solve a constant-coefficient IVP.
ek: Two conditions y(x_0), y′(x_0) fix c_1, c_2.

los.do: Find the roots of the auxiliary equation of an Euler–Cauchy ODE.
ek: x²y″ + axy′ + by = 0 with y = x^m ⇒ m² + (a − 1)m + b = 0.

los.do: Write the general solution of an Euler–Cauchy ODE for each root case and fit an IVP.
ek: Distinct: x^(m₁), x^(m₂); double: x^m, x^m ln x; complex: x^μ cos(ν ln x), x^μ sin(ν ln x).

los.do: Find the natural frequency, period, amplitude and phase of an undamped mass–spring system.
ek: my″ + ky = 0 ⇒ ω₀ = √(k/m); A cos ω₀t + B sin ω₀t = C cos(ω₀t − δ), C = √(A² + B²).

los.do: Solve an undamped oscillator IVP.
ek: y(0) and y′(0) give A and B/ω₀.

los.do: Classify a damped oscillator as over-, critically or underdamped from c² − 4mk.
ek: c² > 4mk overdamped, = critical, < under; underdamped frequency ω* = √(4mk − c²)/2m.

los.do: Solve a damped oscillator IVP in each damping regime.
ek: Same three root cases as 3.2.A, with α = −c/2m < 0 so every solution decays.

los.do: Find a particular solution by undetermined coefficients, including the modification rule.
ek: Guess the form of r(x) (poly, e^(γx), cos/sin); multiply by x (or x²) when the guess solves the homogeneous ODE.

los.do: Assemble y = y_h + y_p and fit an IVP for a nonhomogeneous ODE.
ek: Apply initial conditions to the full solution, never to y_h alone.

los.do: Find a particular solution by variation of parameters when r(x) is not of undetermined-coefficient form or coefficients vary.
ek: y_p = −y₁∫y₂r/W dx + y₂∫y₁r/W dx, ODE in standard form.

los.do: Find the steady-state response of a damped oscillator to sinusoidal forcing and its amplitude.
ek: y_p = a cos ωt + b sin ωt; amplitude C*(ω) = F₀/√((k − mω²)² + c²ω²); the transient dies out.

los.do: Recognise undamped resonance and beats and write the resulting solution.
ek: ω = ω₀, c = 0 ⇒ t sin ω₀t growth; ω near ω₀ ⇒ beats with envelope frequency |ω − ω₀|/2.

los.do: Find the practical-resonance frequency of a damped forced oscillator.
ek: ω_max² = k/m − c²/2m², exists only if c² < 2mk.

los.do: Model an RLC circuit as a second-order ODE and map it onto the mass–spring analogy.
ek: LI″ + RI′ + I/C = E′(t): L ↔ m, R ↔ c, 1/C ↔ k.

los.do: Test n functions for linear independence with the n×n Wronskian.
ek: Rows are f, f′, …, f^(n−1); expand by cofactors.

los.do: Find the roots of an n-th order characteristic polynomial.
ek: Rational root test, then synthetic division to a quadratic.

los.do: Write the general solution of an n-th order constant-coefficient ODE with distinct, repeated and complex roots, and fit an IVP.
ek: A root of multiplicity k gives e^(λx), xe^(λx), …, x^(k−1)e^(λx).

los.do: Find a particular solution of an n-th order ODE by undetermined coefficients or variation of parameters.
ek: Same modification rule; variation of parameters uses Cramer's rule with W_k/W.

units.title: Systems of ODEs, phase plane and stability

los.do: Convert an n-th order ODE into a first-order system.
ek: y₁ = y, y₂ = y′, …; the companion matrix's eigenvalues are the characteristic roots.

los.do: Write the rate matrix for series first-order kinetics A → B → C.
ek: d[A]/dt = −k₁[A], d[B]/dt = k₁[A] − k₂[B]; C follows from mass conservation.

los.do: Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors that give the basis solutions of y′ = Ay.
ek: y = x e^(λt) with (A − λI)x = 0.

los.do: Write the general solution of a 2×2 system with real distinct eigenvalues and fit an IVP.
ek: y = c₁x⁽¹⁾e^(λ₁t) + c₂x⁽²⁾e^(λ₂t).

los.do: Write real solutions of a 2×2 system with complex eigenvalues and fit an IVP.
ek: Take real and imaginary parts of x e^((α+iβ)t).

los.do: Solve a 2×2 system with a repeated eigenvalue using a generalised eigenvector.
ek: Second solution x t e^(λt) + u e^(λt), (A − λI)u = x.

los.do: Solve series kinetics A → B → C and find the time of maximum intermediate.
ek: Eigenvalues −k₁, −k₂; [B] = k₁A₀(e^(−k₁t) − e^(−k₂t))/(k₂ − k₁); t_max = ln(k₁/k₂)/(k₁ − k₂), = 1/k when k₁ = k₂.

los.do: Classify the critical point of a linear 2×2 system (node, saddle, centre, spiral) from its eigenvalues or from trace and determinant.
ek: p = tr A, q = det A, Δ = p² − 4q: q < 0 saddle; q > 0, Δ ≥ 0 node; Δ < 0 spiral (p ≠ 0) or centre (p = 0).

los.do: Decide whether a critical point is stable, asymptotically stable or unstable.
ek: Asymptotically stable ⇔ p < 0, q > 0; centre is stable, not asymptotically.

los.do: Sketch a phase portrait with eigenvector directions and trajectory orientation.
ek: Trajectories leave along the fast-growing eigenvector and approach along the slow-decaying one.

los.do: Find the critical points of a nonlinear autonomous system and linearise at each with the Jacobian.
ek: Set f = g = 0; J = [[f_x, f_y], [g_x, g_y]] at the point.

los.do: Classify each critical point of a nonlinear system from its linearisation, noting when linearisation is inconclusive.
ek: Hyperbolic points keep their type; a linear centre may be a spiral in the nonlinear system.

los.do: Find a particular solution of y′ = Ay + g by undetermined coefficients, diagonalisation or variation of parameters.
ek: Fundamental matrix Y: y_p = Y∫Y⁻¹g dt.

los.do: Classify a point as ordinary, regular singular or irregular singular.
ek: Standard form y″ + py′ + qy = 0: ordinary if p, q analytic; regular singular if (x − x₀)p and (x − x₀)²q are analytic.

los.do: Give the guaranteed radius of convergence of a power-series solution about an ordinary point.
ek: At least the distance to the nearest singular point in the complex plane.

los.do: Derive the recurrence relation for the coefficients of a power-series solution.
ek: Substitute Σa_m x^m, shift indices to a common power, set each coefficient to zero.

los.do: Generate the first terms of the series solution from the recurrence and initial values.
ek: a₀ = y(0), a₁ = y′(0); even and odd coefficients often split into two basis series.

los.do: Find the indicial equation and its roots at a regular singular point.
ek: r(r − 1) + b₀r + c₀ = 0, b₀ = lim xp, c₀ = lim x²q.

los.do: Decide which Frobenius case applies and what form the second solution takes.
ek: Roots not differing by an integer: two x^r series; double root: second has ln x; differ by an integer: second may have ln x.

los.do: Construct the first Frobenius series solution from the larger indicial root.
ek: y = x^r Σa_m x^m; same index-shifting as the power series method.

los.do: Recognise Legendre's, Bessel's and Euler–Cauchy equations in a given ODE and read off the order or degree.
ek: (1 − x²)y″ − 2xy′ + n(n+1)y = 0; x²y″ + xy′ + (x² − ν²)y = 0.

los.do: Solve a scaled Bessel equation x²y″ + xy′ + (λ²x² − ν²)y = 0 with J_ν(λx), Y_ν(λx).
ek: Substitute z = λx.

los.do: Write the general solution of Bessel's equation, choosing J₋ν or Y_ν as the second solution.
ek: J_ν, J₋ν independent unless ν is an integer, where J₋ₙ = (−1)ⁿJₙ; then use Y_ν.

los.do: Use Legendre polynomials' explicit form, Rodrigues' formula or orthogonality to evaluate P_n or an integral.
ek: P_n(x) = (1/2ⁿn!) dⁿ/dxⁿ (x² − 1)ⁿ; ∫P_mP_n = 0 on [−1, 1] for m ≠ n.

los.do: Find the Laplace transform of a combination of elementary functions from the table, using identities where needed.
ek: L{tⁿ} = n!/s^(n+1); L{e^(at)} = 1/(s − a); L{cos ωt} = s/(s² + ω²); sin² = (1 − cos 2t)/2.

los.do: Apply the first shifting theorem forwards and in reverse.
ek: L{e^(at)f(t)} = F(s − a); complete the square to expose s − a.

los.do: Invert a rational F(s) by partial fractions with distinct, repeated or complex poles.
ek: Repeated pole ⇒ tⁿe^(at)/n!; complex pole pair ⇒ e^(at)(cos, sin).

los.do: Solve a constant-coefficient IVP by transforming, solving the subsidiary equation and inverting.
ek: L{y′} = sY − y(0); L{y″} = s²Y − sy(0) − y′(0); initial conditions enter automatically.

los.do: Identify the transfer function of a linear system and relate its poles to stability and damping.
ek: Q(s) = Y/R with zero ICs = 1/(as² + bs + c); poles in the left half-plane ⇔ decay.

los.do: Write a piecewise function with unit step functions and transform it.
ek: f = f₁ + (f₂ − f₁)u(t − a) + …; L{f(t − a)u(t − a)} = e^(−as)F(s).

los.do: Invert a transform containing e^(−as).
ek: e^(−as)F(s) ↦ f(t − a)u(t − a).

los.do: Solve an IVP with switched or piecewise forcing.
ek: Transform the step-written forcing; the solution is piecewise with continuous y and y′.

los.do: Model a sudden impulse with δ(t − a) and solve the resulting IVP, including the impulse response.
ek: L{δ(t − a)} = e^(−as); impulse response = L⁻¹{transfer function}.

los.do: Compute a convolution integral directly.
ek: (f * g)(t) = ∫₀ᵗ f(τ)g(t − τ)dτ.

los.do: Invert a product of transforms or transform an integral using the convolution theorem.
ek: L{f * g} = FG; L{∫₀ᵗ f dτ} = F/s.

los.do: Solve a Volterra integral equation of convolution type.
ek: Transform, solve for Y algebraically, invert.

los.do: Use L{tf(t)} = −F′(s) to transform or invert functions and solve ODEs with linear coefficients.
ek: Differentiation in s ↔ multiplication by −t; integration in s ↔ division by t.

los.do: Solve a linear system of ODEs by Laplace transform.
ek: Transform each equation, solve the algebraic system (Cramer), invert each component.

los.do: Solve a linear system by row reduction and state whether it has none, one or infinitely many solutions.
ek: Echelon form; rank A vs rank [A|b] decides existence; free variables give a family.

los.do: Decide whether a set of vectors is linearly independent.
ek: Independent ⇔ only the trivial combination is zero ⇔ rank = number of vectors; for n vectors in ℝⁿ, det ≠ 0.

los.do: Evaluate a 3×3 determinant by cofactor expansion.
ek: Expand along the row or column with most zeros; sign pattern (−1)^(i+j).

los.do: Find the inverse of a 2×2 matrix, or show it does not exist.
ek: A⁻¹ = (1/det A)[[d, −b], [−c, a]]; singular ⇔ det A = 0.

los.do: Find the eigenvalues of a 2×2 matrix from its characteristic polynomial.
ek: λ² − (tr A)λ + det A = 0.

los.do: Find an eigenvector for each eigenvalue of a 2×2 matrix.
ek: Solve (A − λI)x = 0; one row suffices in 2×2.

los.do: Diagonalise a matrix with a full set of eigenvectors and use it to decouple a linear system.
ek: D = X⁻¹AX; symmetric A has real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors.

units.title: Fourier series and Sturm–Liouville boundary-value problems

los.do: Compute the Fourier coefficients of a 2π-periodic function given on one period.
ek: a₀ = (1/2π)∫f, a_n = (1/π)∫f cos nx, b_n = (1/π)∫f sin nx over (−π, π).

los.do: Compute the Fourier series of a function of period 2L, using even/odd symmetry to skip coefficients.
ek: Replace nx by nπx/L and 1/π by 1/L; even ⇒ cosine series, odd ⇒ sine series.

los.do: Write the half-range sine or cosine expansion of a function on (0, L).
ek: Odd extension ⇒ sine series; even extension ⇒ cosine series; b_n = (2/L)∫₀ᴸ f sin(nπx/L).

los.do: Find the periodic steady-state response of an oscillator to a periodic non-sinusoidal force by Fourier series.
ek: Solve term by term; the term with nω nearest ω₀ dominates.

los.do: Rewrite a second-order eigenvalue ODE in Sturm–Liouville form and identify p, q and r.
ek: (py′)′ + (q + λr)y = 0; multiply by the integrating factor e^(∫a₁/a₂)/a₂ when needed.

los.do: Classify a Sturm–Liouville problem as regular, periodic or singular.
ek: Regular: p > 0, r > 0 on [a, b] with separated BCs; periodic: y(a) = y(b), y′(a) = y′(b); singular: p vanishes at an end.

los.do: Find the eigenvalues of y″ + λy = 0 under Dirichlet, Neumann or mixed boundary conditions.
ek: Check λ < 0, = 0, > 0 separately; Dirichlet on [0, L]: λ = (nπ/L)², n ≥ 1.

los.do: Find the eigenfunction belonging to each eigenvalue.
ek: Determined up to a constant multiple; sin(nπx/L), cos(nπx/L) or sin((2n−1)πx/2L).

los.do: Find the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a shifted problem y″ + (λ + c)y = 0 and count its negative eigenvalues.
ek: Set μ = λ + c, solve as 9.2.C, then λ = μ − c.

los.do: Verify orthogonality of eigenfunctions with respect to the weight r(x).
ek: ∫ₐᵇ r y_m y_n dx = 0 for m ≠ n in a regular or periodic S–L problem.

los.do: Expand a function in a generalised Fourier series of S–L eigenfunctions (e.g. Legendre or Fourier–Bessel).
ek: a_n = ∫ r f y_n dx / ∫ r y_n² dx.

los.do: Classify a second-order linear PDE as elliptic, parabolic or hyperbolic and verify a solution.
ek: Au_xx + 2Bu_xy + Cu_yy: AC − B² > 0 elliptic, = 0 parabolic, < 0 hyperbolic.

topics.title: Heat equation by separation of variables

los.do: Separate u = F(x)G(t) in the heat equation and find each mode's decay rate.
ek: F″ + kF = 0 (an S–L problem), G′ + c²kG = 0 ⇒ G = e^(−c²λ_n t).

los.do: Solve the heat equation on a finite rod with Dirichlet or insulated ends by Fourier series.
ek: Dirichlet ⇒ sine series; insulated ⇒ cosine series with a constant term (the mean).

los.do: Solve the heat equation with non-homogeneous Dirichlet ends by subtracting the steady state.
ek: u = u_s(x) + v; u_s linear; v satisfies zero BCs with v(x, 0) = f − u_s.

los.do: Solve the vibrating string by separation of variables and Fourier series.
ek: u = Σ(B_n cos λ_n t + B_n* sin λ_n t) sin(nπx/L), λ_n = cnπ/L.

los.do: Write d'Alembert's solution for an infinite string from initial displacement and velocity.
ek: u = ½[f(x + ct) + f(x − ct)] + (1/2c)∫ g.

los.do: Solve the steady 2-D Dirichlet problem on a rectangle by separation.
ek: One direction gives sines, the other sinh; one non-zero side at a time, then superpose.

los.do: Separate a PDE in polar, cylindrical or spherical coordinates and identify the Bessel or Legendre equation that appears.
ek: Radial part in cylinders ⇒ Bessel; polar angle in spheres ⇒ Legendre in cos θ.

los.do: Solve a PDE on a semi-infinite or infinite domain by Laplace or Fourier transform.
ek: Transform out t (Laplace) or x (Fourier) to get an ODE in the other variable.

los.do: Represent a non-periodic function by its Fourier integral, or its cosine or sine transform.
ek: Limit L → ∞ of the Fourier series; even ⇒ cosine transform, odd ⇒ sine.

los.do: Compute a Fourier transform and use its derivative property to turn an ODE into algebra.
ek: F{f′} = iwF{f}; F{e^(−ax²)} is Gaussian.

topics.title: Grad, div, curl and the integral theorems

los.do: Compute the gradient, divergence, curl and Laplacian of a field in Cartesian coordinates.
Derive a differential conservation equation from an integral balance with the divergence theorem.
ek: ∭∇·F dV = ∯F·n dA ⇒ ∂c/∂t + ∇·N = R.
